review.reason: Current PyPI/OSV advisory metadata invalidates two additional versions still carried by the proposed TensorFlow 2.21.0 Python 3.11 runtime set: protobuf 6.31.1 and setuptools 78.1.1. Replace them with the smallest fixed versions that remain inside TensorFlow's declared requirements: protobuf 6.33.5 and setuptools 83.0.0. Exact Windows/Linux protobuf wheel identities and the universal setuptools wheel identity are pinned. Execution remains fail-closed because the rest of the selected dependency set still needs complete exact-wheel, native/license/notice, current-advisory and artifact-to-source closure.

sources: PyPI release JSON for protobuf 6.31.1 and 6.33.5
PyPI release JSON for setuptools 78.1.1 and 83.0.0
TensorFlow v2.21.0 exact dependency declaration already pinned by the parent runtime review
authoritative_metadata.advisory_field_semantics: Point-in-time PyPI/OSV release advisory metadata only. An empty vulnerabilities array is not a claim that a release is vulnerability-free.
authoritative_metadata.historical_tensorflow_lock_role: Compatibility reference only; it must not force execution of a version that has acquired a published advisory.

protobuf==6.31.1.summary: Python protobuf JSON ParseDict recursion-depth accounting can be bypassed through nested Any messages, allowing denial of service through recursion exhaustion.

setuptools==78.1.1.summary: MANIFEST.in exclusion matching before 83.0.0 can be bypassed by Unicode normalization differences on normalization-preserving filesystems, potentially packaging an intended-to-be-excluded file into an sdist.

protobuf.source_tag_signature_note: GitHub reports the annotated v33.5 tag as unsigned; record this rather than treating the tag as a build attestation.

selected_windows_x86_64_wheel.tag_compatibility: CPython ABI3 at cp310 is compatible with the repository's CPython 3.11 Windows x86-64 runtime.

selected_linux_x86_64_wheel.tag_compatibility: CPython ABI3 at cp39 and manylinux2014 x86-64 are compatible with the repository's CPython 3.11 Linux x86-64 runtime.

pure_python_wheel_not_selected.reason: The platform-specific ABI3 wheels are the narrower runtime artifacts for the selected Windows/Linux environments; do not silently substitute a different build during evidence execution.

provenance_and_redistribution_boundary.reason_execution_stays_closed: Source tags and release-wheel hashes are pinned, but this review does not assert that the PyPI wheels were reproducibly built from those commits. The remaining runtime dependency/native notice and source-artifact closure must complete before installation.

security_boundary.reason: This slice repairs two additional demonstrated stale selections only. Other direct/transitive packages still require the same current advisory review before runtime execution can be admitted.

closure.next_smallest_testable_direction: Continue the current-advisory plus exact Windows/Linux wheel and license/notice review for the remaining selected TensorFlow/Keras direct and reachable transitive packages, with special attention to native bundles such as libclang, grpcio, numpy, h5py and ml-dtypes. If every required package clears, close TensorFlow wheel-to-source/notice provenance before any installation. Only then allow the bounded no-media FaceSSD GraphDef construction/conversion smoke below RUNNER_TEMP.
